definition: Genie is a world model developed by Google DeepMind that generates interactive virtual worlds.
details: It is a spatiotemporal transformer, a type of neural network that models what appears in each frame and how the scene changes over time. First introduced in 2024, Genie was initially trained on video game footage and could only generate two-dimensional environments. Later versions had higher resolution and increased memory capabilities and could generate three-dimensional environments. Waymo used Genie 3 to create a variant called the Waymo World Model for simulating edge cases for robotaxis. In 2026, Google released Project Genie, a web interface that allows subscribers to use Genie 3. Genie is used in video game design and autonomous vehicles.

explainer.lead: Genie is a Google DeepMind model that turns learned patterns from video into interactive virtual environments. It matters because generated worlds can support video game design and provide simulations for autonomous vehicles.

tiers.eli5: Genie is like an artist who watches lots of game videos and learns how to make a playable scene of their own. The first version could make only flat, two-dimensional worlds, but later versions could make richer three-dimensional ones and remember more.
tiers.practitioner: Genie is applied through generated interactive environments, including the subscriber-facing Project Genie web interface released in 2026. For autonomous-driving work, Waymo adapted Genie 3 into the Waymo World Model to simulate robotaxi edge cases. Version differences matter: the original 2024 model was limited to 2D, while later releases added higher resolution, more memory, and 3D generation.
tiers.paperLevel: Genie is a spatiotemporal transformer world model: spatial modeling captures what appears within each frame, while temporal modeling captures how the scene changes across frames. In plain notation, learned video dynamics -> generated interactive environment. The 2024 system was trained on video game footage and generated only 2D environments; later versions increased resolution and memory and supported 3D.

explainer.example: Waymo used Genie 3 to create the Waymo World Model, a variant that simulates edge cases for robotaxis.

flow: The original Genie learned from video game footage.
Its spatiotemporal transformer modeled frame contents and scene changes over time.
The model generated an interactive two-dimensional environment.
Later versions extended this process to higher-resolution, three-dimensional worlds with increased memory.
explainer.origin: Google DeepMind introduced Genie in 2024, initially training it on video game footage.
explainer.lineage: The original model generated only 2D environments; later versions added higher resolution, increased memory, and 3D generation. Genie 3 subsequently supported both the Waymo World Model and Google's 2026 Project Genie interface.
explainer.whyItMatters: Genie connects learned video dynamics with interactive world generation, providing a basis for game environments and autonomous-vehicle simulation. Its development from 2D to 3D worlds also expanded the kinds of environments it could represent.
